topic: How Lenders Assess a New Business
objective: Explain how lenders approach applications from newer businesses without long trading history.

slides.subheadline: Less history doesn't mean no path forward.

slides.headline: What does it mean?
slides.body: Newer businesses are assessed differently to established ones, lenders often weigh the director's personal credit history, industry experience, and available security more heavily, since there's less trading history to draw on. Some lenders specialise in start-up and early-stage lending.

caption:
Without years of trading history, lenders lean on other signals, the director's personal credit history, relevant industry experience, and whatever security can be offered, to form a view of risk.

Not every lender is set up to assess new businesses, which is where knowing which lenders specialise in this space can make a real difference to your options.
